title: Natural deletions of element-free DNA between human genes and enhancers showed no detectable rise in expression in 730 cell lines; eQTL-adjusted analyses exclude the rise a contact model predicts
abstract: When people carry a natural deletion of DNA with no known function that lies between a gene and its enhancers, we detect no rise in the gene's expression, although a standard contact model predicts a small rise because the enhancers move closer. This matters because one proposed role of junk DNA is to act as a spacer whose length sets enhancer-gene distance; if so, its length would affect expression and fitness, and sequence-based counts of functional DNA would miss it. We used RNA-seq of lymphoblastoid cell lines from 730 people (MAGE) and structural-variant genotypes of the same people (1000 Genomes). For each common deletion and gene within 1 Mb we estimated the expression change per deletion copy. Enhancers and weights came from the activity-by-contact (ABC) model in GM12878 (ABC score = the fraction of a gene's regulatory input from one element). A clean deletion removes no exon, candidate regulatory element, conserved element or ABC element. We predicted each clean deletion's effect from the shorter distances (contact proportional to 1/distance) and regressed observed on predicted effects (slope 1 = model correct, 0 = no effect). Positive control: 374 deletions that remove ABC elements lowered expression with slope 1.31 (95% CI 0.45 to 2.08). Spacer test: 4,761 clean deletions (52,861 gene pairs) gave -0.69 (-1.83 to 0.44) in the pre-specified model and -0.55 (-1.28 to 0.19) after adjustment for each gene's lead eQTL variants. All 27 adjusted variants and 5 of 9 unadjusted variants exclude slope 1 (32 of 36); adjusted upper bounds are at most 0.26, or 0.60 without the 150 pairs within 5 kb of the TSS. For pairs with predicted rises of at least 0.21% (+0.37% on average), unadjusted data gave +0.31% (-0.24 to +0.97), consistent with the model, but adjusted data gave -0.06% (-0.38 to +0.19). Exploratory: deletions of non-repeat clean DNA lowered expression where the model predicted a rise. Limits: most deletions are short (median 299 bp), so a few dozen loci carry the test; 78% of clean deletions are mostly repeat DNA; eQTL adjustment can absorb real effects and the positive control covers only large effects; a noisy predictor biases slopes towards 0; one cell type; short-read genotypes. Two rounds of independent review changed the analysis and claims. We give loci for CRISPR tests.

display.caption: Observed against predicted change in expression per deletion copy (percent). A: deletions that remove GM12878 ABC enhancer elements (positive control) follow the model (slope 1.31). B: clean deletions of element-free DNA between a gene and its enhancers, unadjusted (slope -1.02). C: the same, adjusted for each gene's lead eQTL variants (slope -0.55). Dashed line: model prediction. Points: weighted mean per bin with 95% CI (2-Mb block bootstrap, 20,000 replicates).

A: spacer slope for clean deletions in 36 analysis variants (4 ways to adjust for lead eQTL variants x 3 covariate sets x 3 weightings). The model value is 1; 32 of 36 intervals exclude it, and all 4 exceptions are unadjusted random-effects fits. B: the positive-control slope under the same adjustments; the two strongest adjustments remove it, so their spacer bounds are not calibrated.
Spacer slope in subsets of deletions and in model variants, unadjusted (blue) and adjusted for lead eQTL variants with r2 < 0.8 (orange). Non-repeat deletions give a negative slope (exploratory).

citations.reason: This study found weak length conservation of enhancer-gene DNA across mammals and proposed testing whether expression is insensitive to such distance changes; our human deletion data show that it is, for natural length changes.
Found no extra rarity of short element-free deletions between validated enhancers and genes; our expression result agrees.
